---
title: "Formatters"
subtitle: "Turning a value into the notation it is read in."
description: "Keisen's formatters: numbers, integers, percentages, currency, scientific notation, byte sizes, dates, markup, and substitutions."
---

Each takes `columns` as a required first positional argument and `rows` as a named one.
`columns` is required rather than defaulted because a Typst positional parameter cannot carry a default, so "every column" is written explicitly as `auto`.

| Function | Notable arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `format(columns, function, rows: auto)` | Any `value => content`. The escape hatch the others are built on. |
| `format-cell(columns, function, rows: auto)` | Any `row => content`. Receives the whole input row, hidden columns and `_index` included, for a cell that depends on its neighbours. |
| `format-number(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 2`, `significant: none`, `grouping: 3`, `group-separator: auto`, `decimal-separator: auto`, `scale: 1`, `sign: false`, `rounding: auto`, `negative-zero: false`, `infinity: none`, `prefix`, `suffix`. |
| `format-integer(columns, ..)` | `format-number` with no fractional part. Passing `decimals` is an error. |
| `format-percent(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 1`, `scale: 100`, `symbol: [%]`, `space: true`. |
| `format-currency(columns, ..)` | `currency: "EUR"`, `decimals: auto`, `symbol: auto`, `position: start`, `space: auto`. |
| `format-scientific(columns, ..)` | `decimals: 2`, `exponent: "power"` or `"e"`, `decimal-separator: auto`, `rounding: auto`, `infinity: none`. |
| `format-bytes(columns, ..)` | `base: 1024`, `decimals: 1`, `group-separator: auto`, `decimal-separator: auto`, `rounding: auto`, `infinity: none`. |
| `format-date(columns, ..)` | `pattern: "[year]-[month]-[day]"`. Takes a `datetime` or an ISO-8601 string. |
| `format-markup(columns, ..)` | Evaluates a string of Typst markup. No arguments of its own. |
| `format-nanoplot(columns, ..)` | `plot`, `width: 4em`, `height: 0.8em`, `baseline: 15%`, `domain: auto`. See [Nanoplots](nanoplots.qmd). |
| `substitute-missing(columns, ..)` | `replacement: [--]`. Applies to `none`, empty strings, and `float.nan`. |
| `substitute-zero(columns, ..)` | `replacement: [--]`. Tests the raw value, before any formatter scales or rounds it. |

: Value formatting {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[35,65]"}

A separator left at `auto` is the theme's, through `number-group-separator` and `number-decimal-separator`, so a French or German table sets its convention once with `table-options` rather than on every directive.
An argument written on the directive wins over the theme, as everywhere else.

Only finite numbers are formatted, and an infinite value is an error unless `infinity:` says what to write for one.
What it writes is opaque content, so it takes no part in the decimal alignment of the column around it.
A column holding an infinity cannot be summarised either: aggregations work in `decimal`, which has no infinity, so a total would silently be the total of the other rows.
`columns: auto` leaves such a column out, as it does a nanoplot column, and naming it in `summary-rows` is an error.

All rounding and scaling happen in Typst's `decimal` type, which is fixed-point, so `0.145` at two decimals is not at the mercy of binary representation.
`rounding: "half-up"` matches `calc.round`, and `"half-even"` is implemented in the package for anyone expecting R's behaviour.
`rounding: auto` takes whichever the theme names in `number-rounding`, which is `"half-up"` unless a theme says otherwise.
Substitutions run before formatting, so a gap never reaches a formatter that would refuse it.

`format-cell` is the only formatter that reads the row rather than the value, and it is worth reaching for last: `columns-combine` covers the common case of building one cell from named neighbours, and reads better where it fits.
A summary row is an aggregate of a column with no row behind it, so a cell formatter never applies to one; the summary falls back to whichever plain directive covers the column, and naming one as a summary's own `format:` is an error.
A serialised specification cannot name it either, since its argument is a closure.

`format-currency` knows EUR, GBP, USD, JPY, and CHF, and writes any other currency as its code, since there are more currencies than anyone should hard-code.
`decimals: auto` follows the currency, so a yen figure carries none.
`symbol: auto` and `space: auto` follow it too: the symbol leads against its number, or trails behind a non-breaking space, as each convention writes it.

`format-scientific` counts the exponent off the digits and cuts the mantissa from them rather than computing either, so it keeps the digits the value had and works on magnitudes `decimal` cannot hold, which is what the notation is for.
Rounding that carries into the next power moves the exponent with it, so nothing renders as `10.0 × 10³`.

`format-bytes` counts in 1024s by default and says so with the binary prefixes; `base: 1000` gives the decimal ones.
Bytes themselves are whole, so the smallest unit carries no fractional part.

`format-date` takes a `datetime` or an ISO-8601 string, since that is how a date arrives from a file: `2026-08-14`, `2026-08-14T09:30:00`, or the space-separated spelling exports write, with or without seconds and with or without a trailing `Z`.
A date that does not exist is refused by pre-check rather than handed to `datetime`, which would panic in a grammar the reader did not write.
`pattern` is Typst's own, so anything `datetime.display` accepts works, and Typst reports a pattern it does not.

`format-date` and `format-markup` both produce opaque content, so neither is decimal-aligned: there is no separator in a date to line up on, and a cell of markup is whatever it evaluates to.
